headline: Europe's wind power surges 30% in first half of 2026
meta_description: Europe installed 8.8 GW of new wind power in H1 2026, a 30% jump year-over-year, powering 7 million homes.
summary_short: Europe added 8.8 GW of new wind turbines in the first half of 2026—30% more than the same period last year—enough to power 7 million homes.
body:
Europe installed 8.8 gigawatts of new wind power capacity in the first half of 2026, marking a 30% increase compared to the same period a year earlier. The surge reflects accelerating momentum in the continent's shift toward renewable energy.

The newly added turbines can generate enough electricity to supply approximately 7 million homes, demonstrating the scale of wind's growing contribution to Europe's energy grid. Beyond the raw capacity figures, the installations represent progress toward reducing fossil fuel dependence, with the new generation potential helping to displace imported energy sources that have long anchored Europe's power mix.

The first-half growth suggests wind energy deployment is gathering pace across the continent, even as Europe pursues its broader climate and energy security goals.
quick_facts: 8.8 GW of new wind power added in Europe's first half 2026
Reduces reliance on fossil fuel imports
